dietEvidence.body: The dentition is consistent with herbivory, and other therizinosaurs are interpreted as plant eaters. No gut contents are known; the plants eaten and the jaw mechanics remain inferred.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A small therizinosaur with preserved filamentous integument and a relatively long neck. It is one of the most complete early therizinosaurs.
summary: Beipiaosaurus inexpectus is a therizinosaur from the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China. It preserves filamentous integument and a pygostyle-like cluster of fused caudal vertebrae. Herbivory is inferred from the dentition and from other therizinosaurs; no gut contents are known.

discovery.body: Named by Xu, Tang & Wang, 1999. The record is known from Yixian Formation, Liaoning. A partial skeleton with extensive integument impressions.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: A partial skeleton with extensive integument impressions.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Yixian Formation, Liaoning records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈125–124 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

fossilEvidence.title: Integument and tail
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype preserves filamentous integument and a pygostyle-like cluster of fused caudal vertebrae. Both are direct anatomical evidence; their function and homology are interpreted.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The body is covered in long filaments, the forelimbs are robust, and the skull is small and edentulous.

behaviour.body: The behavioural record is skeletal: the filamentous integument may have had display or thermoregulatory functions, but this is inferred. The pygostyle-like structure’s function is also unresolved. Social behaviour is unknown.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial skeleton with extensive integument impressions. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The integument and tail structure are direct evidence from the holotype. The skull and skeleton are incomplete, the sample is small, and the function of the filamentous covering is unknown.
